text:
For a typical **120V heated blanket**, I’d choose the **[BLUETTI Elite 100 V2](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket)**: its 1,024Wh battery is estimated to run a 150W blanket for about 12 hours, and it’s listed at roughly $380–$500. A 1kWh station is a reasonable target for an overnight run, but the actual time depends on the blanket’s setting and how often it cycles.

If your blanket draws a high, steady load, go bigger: the **[Jackery HomePower 3000](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-blanket/)** is estimated to run a queen blanket averaging 260W for about 9.5 hours. That’s a much more conservative choice, but it will cost and weigh more.

Check the blanket’s wattage label before buying: as a rough guide, **100W for 8 hours** calls for about 1kWh of battery capacity, while **260W for 8 hours** calls for roughly 2.6kWh. A small 300Wh station generally won’t last all night. ([Runtime estimates and sizing](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-blanket/))
